title: The media control link's certificates, issued by the chat server
spec: docs/CALLS.md 'Built (T360b3)' and 'Built (T360b5)'. crewcraft-pki: LINK_LIFETIME_SECS (30 days), Authority::server_certificate_for(name, now, lifetime) and client_certificate(common name, now, lifetime) (client authentication only, fresh P-256 key). media_link::issue_link(data, media_out, media server name, now) makes a new link CA (Authority::create_root, its key never written), a server certificate for the media server and a client certificate for the chat server, each LINK_LIFETIME_SECS, and writes CHAT_LINK_FILES (media-ca.pem, media-client.pem, media-client-key.pem) into data and MEDIA_LINK_FILES (media.pem, media-key.pem, chat-ca.pem) into media_out, owner-only, each replaced in one step; it returns the expiry. The chat server's device CA is never used: every enrolled device holds a client certificate from it. `crewcraft-server media-link-cert <data> <name> <out>` runs it. Operator-supplied PEM files keep working. Test: the issued files exist, owner-only, expiring in 30 days; the pair completes the mutual-TLS link (an event from the chat server's link reaches the media server's intake); a client certificate from another issue is answered with nothing and changes nothing; issuing again replaces the files. The command writes both ends and refuses a bad name.
